This is TD Studios’ luxury website: a Next.js 15.5.4 App Router app with strict TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Radix UI/shadcn (New York, RSC), Geist Sans/Mono, Lucide React, Vercel Analytics, Vitest, and Playwright. The repository syncs v0.app → GitHub → Vercel; major changes should use v0.app. Consider sync implications before direct edits. Project: https://v0.app/chat/projects/MgSVoHLfRb7.

## Structure and routes
- `app/`: pages and API routes; `app/globals.css`, `layout.tsx` (StickyHeader, Footer, analytics, mobile viewport fixes), `page.tsx` (homepage).
- Pages: `/`, `/work`, `/web`, `/dev`, `/social`, `/design`, `/process`, `/resources`, `/faq`, `/contact`, `/book`, `/support`, `/legal`, `/[client]/signin`, `/clients/[client]`.
- `/pricing` merged into `/faq`; `/services` split into `/web`, `/dev`, `/social`, `/design`. See `ROUTES.md`.
- API routes: `api/contact/` (POST, Resend); `api/chatkit/session/` (POST, OpenAI); `api/intake/` (POST, Supabase).
- `components/`: reusable UI, including `sticky-header.tsx`, `nav.tsx`, `footer.tsx`, `glass-card.tsx`, `frosted-button.tsx`, `page-title.tsx`, `section.tsx`, `json-ld.tsx`, `calendly-embed.tsx`, `logo.tsx`, `analytics-provider.tsx`, `ab-test-wrapper.tsx`, `theme-provider.tsx`, and `ui/`.
- `lib/`: `utils.ts` (`cn`), `analytics.ts`, `ab-testing.ts`; `public/` static assets; `styles/`; `tests/` E2E tests and screenshots.
- Primary nav: WORK · WEB · DEV · SOCIAL · DESIGN · PROCESS · RESOURCES · FAQ · CONTACT. Footer: Support · Legal · Book. Pages include canonical, OpenGraph, Twitter Card metadata, and JSON-LD.

## Design and implementation
Luxury, mobile-first aesthetic: dark black background (`oklch(0.145 0 0`), white text, neutral glassmorphism at 70% opacity with backdrop blur, OKLCH design tokens, 0.625rem default radius, responsive spacing, light/dark theme support, accessible hover/focus states, and Lucide icons. `app/globals.css` includes mobile optimizations; `layout.tsx` has an inline iOS Safari viewport/background optimization script. `FrostedButton` supports Link or button and analytics; use consistent glass cards, Tailwind variants, and touch-friendly interactions.

Use strict typing, `@/*` aliases, `"use client"` for interactive components, PascalCase component names and kebab-case files, dedicated props interfaces, ARIA/semantic HTML/keyboard support, lazy loading, code splitting, and optimized re-renders.

## Environment
Create `.env.local` from `.env.local.example`:
- `RESEND_API_KEY`, `CONTACT_TO_EMAIL`
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_TIME` (auto-injected during build)
- `JWT_SECRET` (minimum 32 characters)
- `CLIENT_{CLIENTSLUG}_PASSCODE` (e.g. `CLIENT_THEBODYBOUTIQUE_PASSCODE`)

Client portals use `jose` JWTs signed with `JWT_SECRET`; clients have unique passcodes. `/[client]/signin` authenticates; `/clients/[client]` requires a valid JWT.

## Commands
```sh
pnpm dev
pnpm serve
pnpm build
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm ci:verify
pnpm report:types
pnpm scan:secrets
pnpm scan:secrets:staged
pnpm test
pnpm test:watch
pnpm test:jest
npx playwright test
npx playwright test --ui
npx playwright test tests/mobile-layout.spec.ts
pnpm lh:routes
```
`pnpm ci:verify` runs lint + typecheck + test; use it before commits. `pnpm dev` runs port 3000; `pnpm serve` serves the production build on port 3000. Vitest uses jsdom, `tests/setup.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `*.spec.ts?(x)`, `@/` aliases, automatic JSX, and `passWithNoTests: false`; Playwright tests are excluded (`**/mobile-layout.spec.ts`, `**/playwright/**`). E2E tests focus on mobile layout, hero centering, parallax, touch targets, viewport/text sizing; screenshots in `tests/screenshots/`. Playwright uses default configuration (no custom config file).

## Configuration
Next.js: strict mode; image domains `i.imgur.com`, `via.placeholder.com`, `cdn.platform.openai.com`, `tdstudiosny.com`; AVIF/WebP; permanent 301 redirect `www.tdstudiosny.com` → `tdstudiosny.com`. ESLint errors ignored during builds for deployment compatibility; TypeScript build errors ignored for v0.app integration.
TypeScript: ES2017, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, Next.js plugin, isolated modules, `@/*` root alias.
shadcn: New York, neutral, RSC and CSS variables enabled; aliases for components, utils, ui, lib, hooks.

## Analytics, integrations, dependencies
Track page views, button clicks/location, form success/errors, downloads, bookings, scroll depth, time on page, CTA position. A/B tests support variant definitions, traffic allocation, enable/disable, and analytics conversion tracking. Vercel Analytics and custom tracking utilities are integrated.
API: contact accepts name/email/message and returns email-delivery status; ChatKit creates/continues sessions and returns session token/configuration; intake accepts lead/qualification data, stores qualified leads in Supabase, and returns lead ID/status.
Stack includes React 18, TypeScript 5, Tailwind 3.4.17, React Hook Form/Zod, Supabase, OpenAI, Resend, jose, Sonner, cmdk, Embla, Recharts, react-resizable-panels, Vaul, input-otp, Calendly, ChatKit, date-fns, next-themes, Vitest, Playwright, Jest, Lighthouse, secretlint, Husky, `tsx`, and `start-server-and-test`.

## Git/security workflow
Husky hooks are installed automatically via postinstall. Pre-commit scans staged files for secrets:
```sh
if ! git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | xargs -I{} -r secretlint "{}"; then
echo "🚫 Secretlint found potential secrets in staged files."
```
Pre-push enforces feature branches and scans secrets:
```sh
branch="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
[ "$branch" = "main" ] && { echo "🚫 Direct pushes to main are blocked. Use feature branch + PR."; exit 1; }
if [ -z "$CI" ]; then
pnpm -s scan:secrets >/dev/null || { echo "🚫 Pre-push secret scan failed."; exit 1; }
```
Secretlint uses `<REDACTED_USER>/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend`. Branch protection requires PRs for all changes to main.

## Documentation
`docs/architecture-map.json` documents architecture, stack, infrastructure, DNS/TLS/HTTP, integrations, deployment, security action items, and enhancements. Reference it for onboarding, infrastructure changes, and security audits. Last updated 2025-10-10. UX research covers design, journeys/conversion, luxury-brand standards, and performance.
